newsitem.title: USA: LPC-American Stores taps Morgan for $2 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: LPC-American Stores taps Morgan for $2 bln loan.

text.p: NEW YORK- March 5 (LPC) - J.P. Morgan & Co Inc on Friday began syndicating their $2 billion loan that partially funds American Stores Co $550 million repurchase of 12.2 million shares of common stock, market sources said.
The common shares are held by L.S. Skaggs and certain family and charitable trusts, according a news report.
The deal replaces a $1 billion credit put in place by Morgan in June 1994.

The loan is split between a $500 million, 364-day facility and a $1.5 billion, five-year revolver. Pricing on the shorter tranche, which will be used for the repurchase, is 18.5 basis points over the London Inter-Bank Offered Rate (LIBOR), with a 6.5 basis-point facility fee.

Pricing on the longer tranche, which is tied to ratings, starts at 16.5 basis points over LIBOR, with an 8.5-basis-point facility fee. The bulk of the credit will be used for general corporate purposes.
Commitments are due March 20. Pricing on the 1994, five-year revolver started at LIBOR plus 35 basis points, with a 12.5-basis-point facility fee and a five-basis-point commitment fee.
